newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Ortiz says Mexican domestic consumption improving.
newsitem.headline: Ortiz says Mexican domestic consumption improving.

text.p: Mexican Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz said on Friday that there were signs that domestic consumption was picking up and it could help push up economic growth in 1997.
Until now, Mexico's recovery from the economic crisis of 1995 had been led by investment and exports.
"Consumption will be better in 1997. We have forecasts for a growth of 2.5 percent," he told a news conference at the World Economic Forum.
He said the hopeful signs for domestic consumption meant that economic growth could turn out to be higher than the programmed four percent for 1997, he added.
He earlier told Reuters Television that growth in 1997 could be above the programmed four percent. Gross Domestic Product (GDP) was expected to have expanded 4.6 percent last year.

Ortiz said that he was not concerned about the rise of the Mexican peso because Mexico's exports were not particularly currency sensitive. In any case, most of the country's trade was with the United States and the dollar was also strong.
The minister said that the government had no target for the peso even if the market was expecting around 8.5 pesos to the dollar in 1997. The Mexican currency closed at 7.83 on Thursday.
